about: The parity contract for the runner protocol (#243): one case per rule, and the
verdict every implementation of this wire format has to produce for it.
The agent is Go (AG.2, #244) and the gateway is TypeScript (AH.3, #251); the fake
agent that drives the gateway's suite is TypeScript too (AH.7, #255). All three read
this directory directly. That is what makes them agree without any of them importing
another: a rule added to one and forgotten in the next is a failure in the half that
was forgotten, on the pull request that forgot it.
A diagnostic is recorded as its `code` and the RFC 6901 `path` it is anchored at. Its
message is not: each implementation renders its own prose, and a contract over English
sentences is one nobody can translate. Diagnostics are in document order -- by path,
with numeric path segments compared as numbers, then by code.
An envelope error ends the walk. A frame whose envelope does not decode has no
payload to check, so every envelope case below carries exactly one diagnostic --
reporting a second would mean guessing which message type the payload was meant to
be.
The 32768-byte chunk cap is NOT a fixture. It is published as a number in
`../v1.json` under `$defs/limits`, and each implementation constructs the boundary
case from it in a unit test -- which is the same assertion without 88KB of base64 in
git.
Regenerating this file is not how it is maintained. It is reviewed and frozen; a
change to it is a change to the contract, and every suite has to be green on the new
one.

cases.name: hello
cases.about: The first message. Identity is the TLS client certificate (#250), so no token travels here.

cases.name: hello-resume
cases.about: The same message after a drop, naming the session it wants back.

cases.name: hello-bearer-fallback
cases.about: Decision B3's degraded mode, REPORTED rather than hidden: the gateway records it in the runner row and the farm page shows it (#244, #257). The bearer secret itself travels in the upgrade request, never in a frame.

cases.name: hello-without-security-mode
cases.about: `security_mode` was added inside line 1, so it is optional and a hello without it is still legal (§ 3). The gateway reads the transport instead.

cases.name: ack
cases.about: The session, the negotiated protocol, every limit the agent must not hard-code, and the pool's execution policy (#246).

cases.name: ack-resumed
cases.about: The same answer when the session survived the drop.

cases.name: ack-without-pool
cases.about: `pool` was added inside line 1 (#246), so it is optional and an ack without it is still legal (§ 3). The agent assumes the pool column defaults: one job at a time, and no variable allowed through.

cases.name: refuse
cases.about: The version floor, with the minimum named so the refusal is actionable.

cases.name: heartbeat
cases.about: Idle presence: no job, and `job` is null rather than absent.

cases.name: heartbeat-busy
cases.about: The same message with a job in it -- the row the farm table renders.

cases.name: heartbeat-unmeasured
cases.about: A machine that cannot measure itself says so: each measurement null, never 0 and never the last value it read -- and the runners table draws an em-dash (#245, #257). Also the first beat after an agent starts, before a CPU window has closed.

cases.name: job-offer
cases.about: A container job: the executor that requires an image.

cases.name: job-offer-shell
cases.about: A shell job: the executor that forbids one, on the darwin/arm64 pool.

cases.name: job-accept
cases.about: Taken -- naming the offer envelope, so a re-offer cannot be answered twice.

cases.name: job-decline
cases.about: Refused, with a reason the dispatcher can act on rather than a silence it must time out.

cases.name: job-start
cases.about: Running, with the attempt number that makes a retry distinguishable from a re-send.

cases.name: job-progress
cases.about: Advisory only: a job that sends none is not a job that has stopped.

cases.name: job-finish
cases.about: The terminal message. Its envelope id IS its idempotency id.

cases.name: job-finish-failed
cases.about: The same message for a failure: an exit code, an error, and no ccache statistics.

cases.name: log-chunk
cases.about: Output, base64 because build logs are bytes and JSON strings are text.

cases.name: receipt
cases.about: The acknowledgement that lets the agent stop re-sending.

cases.name: receipt-duplicate
cases.about: The same acknowledgement for a frame already recorded -- how an agent learns its re-send was deduplicated rather than lost.

cases.name: drain
cases.about: Withdrawn from dispatch, with the deadline the operator is promising.

cases.name: undrain
cases.about: Back in rotation. An empty payload is an object, never an absence.

cases.name: bye
cases.about: The orderly close -- what a SIGTERM becomes.

cases.name: envelope-not-object
cases.about: A frame that is not an object at all.

cases.name: envelope-version-missing
cases.about: The version is present from message one, which is the one thing that cannot be retrofitted.

cases.name: envelope-version-type
cases.about: `v` is an integer. A string that looks like one is not one.

cases.name: envelope-version-unsupported
cases.about: A line this implementation does not speak. Rejected as a version, not as a bad field.

cases.name: envelope-type-missing
cases.about: No type, so there is no payload contract to apply.

cases.name: envelope-type-unknown
cases.about: A type outside the enum. The walk stops rather than guessing what was meant.

cases.name: envelope-id-missing
cases.about: Without an id a terminal frame cannot be deduplicated, so every frame carries one.

cases.name: envelope-id-malformed
cases.about: An id that is not a ULID. The shape is fixed so ids sort by the time they were minted.

cases.name: envelope-payload-missing
cases.about: A payload is always present, even when it is empty.

cases.name: envelope-payload-type
cases.about: The payload is an object. An array is not an object.

cases.name: envelope-field-unknown
cases.about: The envelope is frozen across every version, so a fifth key is an error rather than an extension point.

cases.name: hello-arch-enum
cases.about: An architecture outside the three the fleet builds for.

cases.name: hello-protocol-range
cases.about: There is no protocol 0. The advertised range starts at 1.

cases.name: hello-hostname-missing
cases.about: An agent with no hostname is a row nobody can identify in the runners table.

cases.name: hello-field-unknown
cases.about: An enrollment token does NOT travel in `hello` (#250). A frame that carries one is refused, which is what keeps a bearer secret out of every session log.

cases.name: hello-security-mode-enum
cases.about: A security mode outside decision B3's two. There is no third way to authenticate, and a frame claiming one is refused rather than recorded.

cases.name: ack-pool-concurrency-range
cases.about: A pool that lets a runner hold no jobs at all. `max_concurrency` is 1-64, the bounds `runner_pools` holds it to (#249); zero is a pool that could never run anything.

cases.name: heartbeat-cpu-range
cases.about: A percentage above 100.

cases.name: heartbeat-cpu-missing
cases.about: Null, not absent: a measurement this machine cannot take is sent as null, and a heartbeat without the key has two shapes for one message.

cases.name: heartbeat-state-enum
cases.about: A state the control plane has no column for.

cases.name: job-offer-image-conflict
cases.about: An image on a shell job. Not merely ignored -- refused, because a dispatcher that sent one meant a container.

cases.name: job-offer-image-missing
cases.about: A container job with nothing to run in.

cases.name: job-offer-command-type
cases.about: The command is an argv array, never a shell string -- there is no shell to split it.

cases.name: job-finish-exit-missing
cases.about: An outcome that ran has an exit code.

cases.name: job-finish-outcome-enum
cases.about: An outcome outside the five the control plane records.

cases.name: job-finish-exit-null
cases.about: `succeeded` with a null exit code. Not a missing field -- the key is there, and it says the command never ran, which the outcome contradicts.

cases.name: log-chunk-data-not-base64
cases.about: A `data` that is not base64. Reported as a type error rather than a range one: it is not a chunk of the wrong size, it is not a chunk.

cases.name: log-chunk-seq-range
cases.about: Sequence numbers are 0-based and contiguous, which is what makes ordering checkable.

cases.name: log-chunk-encoding-enum
cases.about: base64 is the only encoding. A build log is bytes, and not every byte sequence is text.

cases.name: two-mistakes
cases.about: Ordering, and it is not code order: `payload.field.range` at /payload/cpu_pct comes before `payload.field.enum` at /payload/state, because diagnostics sort by path first.

transcripts.name: enroll
transcripts.about: The enrollment card's sentence, frame by frame.

transcripts.name: resume
transcripts.about: A terminal frame re-sent after a drop. Exactly one duplicate, and exactly one finished job.

transcripts.name: refuse
transcripts.about: The version floor, refused and closed.
